audience: New Finance users who reconcile a bank account in Odoo Accounting.
goal: Key two lines from a bank statement into the **Commercial Bank** journal, **reconcile** a customer cheque against the invoice it pays, post a bank charge to the expense account, validate both entries, and finish by proving the closing balance with the **Reconciliation Report**.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app and post bank entries.
You have the bank statement in front of you: for every line, the date, the narration the bank printed, and the amount.
A **Commercial Bank** journal exists in Odoo.
For the cheque: the customer's invoice is posted and still unpaid, and you know its number.
outcome: Both statement lines are saved and reconciled (each shows a green tick in the list).
The customer's invoice is shown as paid.
The bank charge is posted as an expense on **72030110 BANK CHARGES**.
The Reconciliation Report agrees with the bank statement.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. Records created by the run carry a **[TEST]** prefix and a short random code in their label, and the invoice number may differ from the example in the text (**FTI/2026/00355**). Use your own statement values and invoice number.
The red banner at the top of the screenshots ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases.

phases.title: Find your bank journal
phases.summary: Open the Accounting dashboard and locate the right bank card before you touch anything.
phases.checkpoint: You can see the **Commercial Bank** card and have read its three figures.

phases.title: Key in the bank statement lines
phases.summary: Enter a customer cheque (money in) and a bank charge (money out) exactly as the bank shows them.
phases.checkpoint: Two new lines — the **600** cheque receipt and the **−1,500** bank charge — are saved in the Commercial Bank journal.

phases.title: Open the reconciliation workspace
phases.summary: Learn the screen where every unmatched bank line is worked through, one at a time.
phases.checkpoint: You are on the **Bank Reconciliation** screen with the bank charge selected, and you know why Bank Suspense is shown.

phases.title: Post the bank charge
phases.summary: A charge has no invoice behind it, so it is posted straight to an expense account.
phases.checkpoint: The bank charge shows a **green tick** — it is reconciled and posted to 72030110 BANK CHARGES.

phases.title: Match the customer cheque to its invoice
phases.summary: Replace the holding account with the customer's actual invoice so the invoice is cleared.
phases.checkpoint: The cheque receipt is reconciled against the invoice, which is now paid.

phases.title: Prove the balance
phases.summary: Open and read the Reconciliation Report that shows the bank account agrees with the bank.
phases.checkpoint: You have read the **Reconciliation Report** and, if you wanted one, saved a copy.

glossary.meaning: A book in which Odoo records one kind of transaction. Each bank account has its own bank journal (here **Commercial Bank**).
One row on the bank's statement: a date, a narration and an amount. It must exist in Odoo before it can be reconciled.
Match a bank line with the accounting entry that explains it (an invoice, a payment or an expense) so that Odoo's balance agrees with the bank's.
A holding account (**12090250**) that Odoo uses until you say what a bank line really was. Reconciling means replacing it with the correct account or invoice.
The customer or supplier a line belongs to. Setting it makes Odoo offer only that partner's open items.
Posts the journal entry and marks the bank line as matched. **To Check** instead sends the line to a colleague for review.
A payment already registered in Odoo that has not yet been matched to a bank line.
The month-end report that starts from the general-ledger balance and explains the difference to the last bank statement.

1.do: Click **Dashboard** in the top menu bar of the Accounting app.
1.see: A set of cards, one for every journal, including each bank account.
1.tip: If you only see a grid of app icons, you are not inside Accounting yet — open the **Accounting** app first, then click Dashboard.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Dashboard**.

2.do: Scroll down and find the card named **Commercial Bank**.
2.see: A card titled **Commercial Bank** with the three figures and the action buttons (New Transaction, Reconcile).
2.warning: Check the name on the card every time. Each bank account has its own card, and reconciling the wrong one posts entries to the wrong account.
actions: Scroll down the dashboard to the bank cards.
Find the card named **Commercial Bank**.
Read the name carefully before going on.

3.do: Read the three figures on the card. You do not need to click anything.
points: **Balance** — what Odoo has posted for this bank account.
**Last Statement** — the closing balance of the last statement you entered.
**Payments** — money registered in Odoo that the bank has not shown yet.
**Reconciliation** is the work of making Balance agree with the real bank statement.
actions: Look at the three figures on the card: Balance, Last Statement and Payments.
Do not click anything yet.

4.do: On the Commercial Bank card, click **New Transaction**.
4.see: A **New Transaction** window with Date, Label, Partner, Amount and Journal.
4.tip: Have an electronic statement from the bank? Use **Import File** instead of keying lines by hand.
actions: On the Commercial Bank card, find the **New Transaction** link.
Click it.
A **New Transaction** window opens.

5.do: Enter the statement date in the **Date** field.

enter.value: Today's date, in the date format your Odoo uses

5.tip: Use the date printed against the line on the bank statement. If the field does not accept what you typed, check the day/month order your Odoo uses.
actions: Click the **Date** field.
Type the statement date (today's date for this exercise) in your Odoo's date format.
Press **Tab** to confirm it.

6.do: Type the bank's narration into the **Label** field.
6.tip: Keep the customer name or cheque number in the label. Odoo reads it when it looks for a matching invoice.
actions: Click the **Label** field.
Type the narration exactly as the bank printed it.
Keep the customer name or cheque number in it.

7.do: Start typing the customer name in **Partner**, then **pick it from the list**.
7.see: The full customer name is shown in the Partner field.
7.tip: Typing alone is not enough — choose the name from the dropdown so the partner is really set.
actions: Click the **Partner** field.
Start typing the customer name.
Choose the customer from the list that appears.

8.do: Type the amount in the **Amount** field.
points: A **positive** number is money received into the account.
A **negative** number is money paid out of the account.
8.warning: Check the sign before you save. A wrong sign is the most common keying mistake on bank statements.
actions: Click the **Amount** field.
Type **600** — a positive number, because money was received.
Press **Tab**.

9.do: Read the **Journal** field. It should say **Commercial Bank**. Nothing to type.
9.warning: A line keyed into the wrong bank journal has to be deleted and entered again, so check it before saving.
actions: Look at the **Journal** field.
Confirm it says **Commercial Bank**.

10.see: The first line is stored and a blank New Transaction window opens for the next line.
10.tip: A statement usually has several lines. Use **Save & Close** only on the last one.
actions: Click **Save & New** at the bottom of the window.
Wait for a blank window to appear for the next line.

11.do: Check the **Date** of the second line, and correct it if needed.

enter.value: The same statement date as the first line

11.tip: Odoo keeps the date you used last. Confirm it is still the statement date.
actions: Look at the **Date** field of the new, blank window.
Check it is still the statement date; type it again if not.

12.do: Type the charge description in **Label** and leave **Partner** empty.
12.tip: A bank charge is not owed to a customer or supplier, so there is no invoice behind it and no partner to set.
12.where: New Transaction window > Label and Partner
actions: Click **Label** and type **Bank charges - September**.
Leave **Partner** empty.

13.do: Type the amount as a **negative** number.
13.see: The amount shows as a negative figure, because money left the account.
13.warning: The minus sign is what tells Odoo the money left the bank account.
actions: Click **Amount**.
Type **-1500** — with the minus sign, because money left the account.
Press **Tab**.

14.see: The window closes. Both transactions are now stored in the Commercial Bank journal, waiting to be reconciled.
actions: Check the three fields once more: Date, Label and Amount.
Click **Save & Close**.
The window closes.

15.do: Open the reconciliation workspace for Commercial Bank. If you are still on the dashboard, click **Reconcile** on the card.
15.see: The **Bank Reconciliation** screen, with your unmatched transactions listed on the left.
15.tip: The number on the Reconcile button is how many bank transactions still have no accounting counterpart. Some versions open this screen straight after saving, so you may already be here.
15.where: Accounting Dashboard > Commercial Bank card > Reconcile
actions: If the dashboard is showing, click **Reconcile** on the Commercial Bank card.
If the **Bank Reconciliation** screen is already open, carry on to the next step.

16.do: Look at the filters in the search bar at the top. Nothing to click.
16.tip: So you only see Commercial Bank lines that still need work. Remove the Not Matched filter later to review lines you have already reconciled.
actions: Look at the search bar at the top.
Read the filter tags shown in it.

17.do: Look at the **Balance** at the top of the left-hand list.
17.tip: At month end this figure must equal the closing balance printed on the bank statement. That is the proof that your reconciliation is complete.
17.where: Bank Reconciliation screen > left-hand list > Balance
actions: Look at the top of the left-hand list.
Read the **Balance** figure.

18.do: Look at the list of unmatched transactions on the left. The selected line is the one you work on.
18.see: Your two lines — the bank charge (−1,500.00) and the cheque receipt (600.00) — in the list. Select the **bank charge** to continue.
18.tip: You work down this list one line at a time.
actions: Look at the list on the left.
Find your two lines: the bank charge (−1,500.00) and the cheque receipt (600.00).
Click the **bank charge** to select it.

19.do: Read the journal entry shown in the top-right panel. Nothing to click.
points: One side is the bank account **12090030 Commercial Bank**.
The other side is **12090250 BANK SUSPENSE**, a holding account used until you say what the transaction really was.
**Reconciling means replacing Bank Suspense** with the correct account or invoice.
actions: Look at the entry in the top-right panel.
Find the bank account **12090030 Commercial Bank** and **12090250 BANK SUSPENSE**.

20.do: Click the **Manual Operations** tab below the entry.
points: **Manual Operations** — post the line straight to an account (used here for the bank charge).
**Match Existing Entries** — match invoices and payments.
**Discuss** — leave a note for a colleague on the line.
20.tip: A bank charge has no invoice to match, which is why Manual Operations is the right tab.
20.where: Bank Reconciliation screen > tabs > Manual Operations
actions: Find the three tabs below the entry.
Click **Manual Operations**.

21.do: In the **Account** field, replace **Bank Suspense** with the expense account.
21.see: The Account field now shows 72030110 BANK CHARGES.
actions: Click the **Account** field and clear it.
Choose **BANK CHARGES** from the list.

22.do: Read the entry before you validate it. Nothing to click.
22.see: **Commercial Bank** against **72030110 BANK CHARGES** for 1,500.00. Bank Suspense is gone.
22.warning: Read both lines and the amount now. Once you validate, this becomes a posted journal entry.
actions: Read both lines of the entry.
Check the account is **72030110 BANK CHARGES** and the amount is 1,500.00.

23.see: Odoo posts the entry, the charge shows a green tick, and the next unmatched transaction is selected.
23.tip: Not sure about a line? Click **To Check** instead, so a colleague can review it.
actions: Click **Validate** (top left of the entry panel).
Wait for the green tick to appear next to the bank charge.

24.do: Confirm Odoo has moved on to the cheque receipt. Nothing to click.
24.see: The **600.00** receipt from **KURUNEGALA CASH CUSTOMER** is selected, and Odoo has already proposed the customer's receivable account **12020010 DEBTORS LEDGER CONTROL** as the counterpart.
24.tip: Odoo can propose this because the line has a partner — that is why setting the partner in step 7 matters.
actions: Look at the left-hand list.
Check the cheque receipt (600.00) is now the selected line.
Note the account Odoo proposes: **12020010 DEBTORS LEDGER CONTROL**.

25.tip: Posting to the receivable account alone would leave the customer's invoice still showing as unpaid. Matching the real invoice makes the receipt clear it.
25.where: Bank Reconciliation screen > tabs > Match Existing Entries
actions: Click the **Match Existing Entries** tab below the entry.

26.do: Look at the filter shown in the tab's search box. Nothing to click yet.
26.see: The list is filtered to the customer, so you only see that customer's open items.
26.tip: If your invoice does not appear, remove the **Partner** filter and search by invoice number. If the bank line had no partner, search by amount or invoice number instead.
26.where: Match Existing Entries tab > search box
actions: Look at the search box inside the tab.
Read the filter tag shown there.

27.do: Type the invoice number the customer is paying into the search box and press **Enter**.

enter.value: FTI/2026/00355 (the number of the invoice your customer is paying)

27.tip: Searching is safer than scrolling when a customer has many open items.
27.where: Match Existing Entries tab > search box
actions: Click the search box in the tab.
Type the invoice number, for example **FTI/2026/00355**.
Press **Enter**.

28.do: Click the invoice's own line — the one on account **12020010 DEBTORS LEDGER** with the invoice number.
28.see: The line is highlighted in the list.
28.warning: The list can also show an **outstanding customer payment** already registered for the same invoice (a different account). Pick that one only if the customer's receipt was already registered as a payment in Odoo — in that case you match the payment line instead of the invoice line.
actions: Look at the rows in the list.
Find the row on account **12020010 DEBTORS LEDGER** that carries your invoice number.
Click that row.

29.do: Check that the invoice is now the counterpart. Nothing to click.
29.see: The suspense proposal is replaced by the invoice's receivable line (**12020010 DEBTORS LEDGER**) for 600.00, with the invoice number underneath. Nothing is left over.
29.tip: If the receipt were smaller than the invoice, Odoo would keep the difference open and the invoice would show as partially paid.
actions: Look at the entry in the top-right panel.
Check the receivable line shows your invoice and 600.00, with nothing left over.

30.see: Odoo posts the entry, marks the invoice as paid, and the bank line is no longer in the Not Matched list.
30.tip: Odoo can take a few seconds to apply this — wait for the green tick before moving on, and do not click Validate twice.
actions: Click **Validate**.
Wait for the green tick — Odoo can take a few seconds.

31.do: Check the result. Nothing to click.
31.see: The counter has dropped by the two lines you reconciled and Odoo moves on to the next unmatched line. If nothing else is waiting, Odoo shows **"Congrats, you're all done!"**.
31.tip: In real use, keep working down the list until the counter reaches zero for the statement period.
actions: Look at the counter at the top, or the message in the middle of the screen.
Confirm Odoo shows **"Congrats, you're all done!"** or moves to the next line.

32.do: Click **Dashboard** in the top menu to go back to the journal cards.
32.tip: Reconciling is not finished until you can prove the bank account agrees with the bank — the next steps do that.
actions: Click **Dashboard** in the top menu bar.

33.do: On the Commercial Bank card, click the **three dots (⋮)** at the top right.
33.see: A menu with the statements, reconciliation models and reports for this bank account.
33.where: Accounting Dashboard > Commercial Bank card > three-dots menu
actions: Find the **Commercial Bank** card.
Click the **three dots (⋮)** at its top-right corner.

34.tip: This is the report you print for the auditor and for month end.
34.where: Commercial Bank card menu > Reconciliation > Reconciliation Report
actions: Find the **Reconciliation** group in the menu.
Click **Reconciliation Report**.

35.do: Read the report from top to bottom. Nothing to click.
points: It starts from the balance of the bank account in the **general ledger**.
Then it shows the **last statement balance**.
Then every **unreconciled receipt and payment** that explains the difference. Unfold a line to see the transactions behind it.
35.see: When nothing is left unreconciled, the two balances agree and Commercial Bank is reconciled.
35.tip: Any warnings at the top (for example about unposted entries or an unexplained difference) tell you what still needs attention.
actions: Read the report from the top down.
Click the small arrows to unfold any line you want to look into.

36.do: To keep a copy, click **PDF** or **XLSX** at the top left of the report.
36.see: A file saved for your month-end folder or for the auditor.
36.tip: That completes the cycle: enter the bank line, match it, validate it, then prove the balance with this report.
actions: Look at the buttons at the top-left of the report.
Click **PDF** or **XLSX** to save a copy.
